subject: GPU runway and activation cadence — Catalyx Therapeutics
messages:
From: Emma Larson <emma@catalyx.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@catalyx.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask + timeline (Catalyx)

Hi Ben / Markus,

Thanks again for the demo — the team was impressed with the latency guarantees and the rollout tooling. We're preparing an internal ask for a dedicated reservation and need a short set of options to present to finance and infra. High level:

- Target initial sustained throughput: ~200 concurrent generation requests (avg 1.2k tokens/req).
- Peak bursts up to ~2.5x sustained during experiments.
- Production SLA expectation: 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints.
- Data residency: US only.

Could you slip us 2–3 concrete capacity options with: cluster size (GPUs), minimum guaranteed GPUs, recommended ramp schedule (first 3 quarters), and a quick note on warm-start / prewarm strategy?

We attached our procurement timetable and RFP (Catalyx_RFP_Dedicated_v2.pdf). Ideally we'd like a pilot in mid-Jan and a production commit by end of Q1.

Appreciate concise options we can pass to finance.

Thanks,
Emma Larson
VP, AI Platforms
Catalyx Therapeutics

Attachment: Catalyx_RFP_Dedicated_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Emma Larson <emma@catalyx.ai>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, procurement@catalyx.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + timeline (Catalyx)

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and the RFP. Per your ask, I've sketched three options below. I've kept costs as ballpark monthly committed-GPU ranges to make finance comparisons straightforward; we'll finalize numbers once you confirm preferred cluster topology and burst policies. Attached: Catalyx_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf with a one-page matrix and quick TCO assumptions.

Option A — Conservative / Fast-start pilot
- Cluster: 8xA100-80GB equivalent nodes (single shard)
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 8 (all reserved)
- Burst capacity: up to +50% on shared burst pool (best-effort)
- Ramp: Pilot (Jan) -> Production MPP (Mar): keep 8 for Q1, evaluate growth.
- Warm strategy: small warm pool (1–2 prewarmed instances per model family), + KV prefix caching.
- Ideal when you want low initial commitment and quick pilot.

Option B — Balanced / predictable throughput (recommended)
- Cluster: 24xA100-80GB equivalent (3 shards of 8)
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 16 (reserved); 8 held as hot standby for burst
- Burst capacity: +2x sustained via pre-provisioned burst lane and queuing priority
- Ramp: Month 0–2: 16; Month 3–6: 20; Month 7–12: 24 (step-up increments tied to adoption triggers)
- Warm strategy: segmented warm pools by workload, automatic prefix/KV cache warmups, and canary lane for new models.
- Notes: balances unit-cost and latency SLOs; fits a production rollout by end of Q1.

Option C — Aggressive / runway for experimentation
- Cluster: 48xA100-80GB equivalent (6 shards of 8)
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 32
- Burst capacity: +3x sustained with dedicated burst lane and reserved burst credits
- Ramp: Month 0: 24 (pilot staging); Month 1–3: 32; Month 4+: 48 as adoption matures
- Warm strategy: large warm pools, elastic prewarming, and priority routing for experiments to avoid noisy neighbor impact
- Notes: higher unit costs but eliminates cold-start risk and supports large parallel experiments.

Operational considerations (quick):
- Canary & rollback: all options support canaries and traffic-splitting with automatic fallback to hosted variants.
- Cost levers: quantization profiles for dev/test, aggressive batching during non-peak windows, and model pruning for experimental branches.
- SLA / monitoring: we can provide per-route p95/p99 latency dashboards, token-level spend, and alerting on KV-cache hit drops.

Next steps: If any of these look viable, I can run a quick cost model tied to your usage profile and produce a final proposal (inc. legal/terms for reserved capacity). Would you prefer the Balanced option as a starting point?

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: Catalyx_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, Emma Larson <emma@catalyx.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, procurement@catalyx.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + timeline (Catalyx)

Emma / Ben — quick technical addendum on expected warmup cost and prewarming cadence: 

- Model families: if you plan to serve 3 model families (search, summarization, policy), prewarming each shard for all families increases memory usage by ~8–12% per shard. Expect a one-time warmup spike (3–6 hours) when promoting from pilot to production.
- KV cache: we recommend a two-stage cache population: (1) synthetic offline population prior to go-live for top N prefixes, (2) live ramp with automated backfill. This reduces p99 latency variance early in rollout.
- Canary sizing: reserve a small dedicated canary lane (2–4 GPUs) to test model variants at production traffic levels.
- Prewarm automation: Redwood's runtime supports prewarm hooks (warmup script that requests representative prompts at controlled TPS). Using this reduces the need for large always-on warm pools and cuts monthly burn by ~6–9% depending on model size.

Operational ask for procurement: we will need a target start date and preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) to lock activation windows for the GPU capacity. For US-only data residency we'll place the fleet in our primary us-west region.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Inference Ops
markus_klein@redwood.com

Hi Ben / Markus — this is great, thanks. A couple quick clarifications from procurement and infra: 

1) Procurement asks whether the Balanced option can be staged with a contractual staircase (16 guaranteed -> 24 guaranteed at month 6) rather than a month-by-month add-on. That suits our approval flow.
2) Infra wants the canary lane explicitly priced as a minimal reserved lane (2 GPUs) rather than ad-hoc.
3) Can you confirm that production commit by end of Q1 would allow us to hit a mid-Jan pilot if we sign the SOW by Dec 15?

If you can update the one-pager with the staircase language and an explicit canary reserve line, we can take it to finance this week. Also, please include estimated monthly committed GPU ranges (ballpark $/GPU/mo) so procurement can model cashflow.

If possible, deliver an updated one-pager by EOD Wednesday so we can circulate it before our Friday exec review.

Best,
Emma
Emma Larson
VP, AI Platforms
Catalyx Therapeutics
